message.content:
Below is a **`gcloud`** CLI command you can run locally (or inside a shell script) to spin up a new Compute‑Engine VM on Google Cloud Platform that meets your requirements:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"
ZONE="us-central1-b"

# NOTE:
#   • Google Compute Engine does NOT offer NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs at present.
#     Available options are Tesla series (T4, P4, V100, K80, A100).
#
#   • To approximate “RTX A6000” performance you would typically choose either
#       – nvidia-a100-series (the newest Ampere architecture)
#       – or nvidia-tesla-v100 if you prefer older Volta hardware.
#
#   • Adjust `MACHINE_TYPE`, `ACCELERATOR_COUNT`, and `GPU_TYPE`
#     according to your budget / performance needs.

# Choose one of the following GPU types:
#   - nvidia-a100-series      # Ampere A100 (best performance)
#   - nvidia-tesla-v100       # Older Volta V100
#   - nvidia-tesla-p4         # Lower cost, lower perf
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a100-series"
ACCELERATORS_PER_INSTANCE=1    # Number of GPUs per VM

# Machine type (CPU + RAM). Pick something that supports the selected GPU.
# Example: n1-highmem-32 has 32 vCPUs & 208 GB memory.
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-highmem-32"

# Boot disk size (GB) and OS image
DISK_SIZE_GB=500
OS_IMAGE_URI="projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-focal"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --boot-disk-size="${DISK_SIZE_GB}"gb \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-focal \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --metadata startup-script='#! /bin/bash
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential dkms linux-headers-$(uname -r)' \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --accelerators=count=${ACCELERATORS_PER_INSTANCE},type=$GPU_TYPE \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure=true
```

### What’s happening?

| Parameter | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU+RAM allocation. Use a high‑memory type (`n1-highmem-*`) because GPUs often pair best with more memory. |
| `--accelerators` | Adds the requested GPU(s). Replace `$GPU_TYPE` with `nvidia-a100-series` or another supported type. |
| `--image-family` | Installs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS automatically. |
| `startup-script` | Installs kernel headers so drivers compile correctly after reboot. |

---

#### Why *not* RTX A6000?

Google Cloud only offers NVIDIA GPUs under the **Tesla** brand (e.g., V100, A100). There isn’t an official RTX A6000 SKU yet. If you specifically need RTX A6000, consider running a bare‑metal host via [GKE Bare Metal](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/bare-metal/) or renting physical servers elsewhere.

Feel free to tweak the values above—especially `MACHINE_TYPE`, `GPU_TYPE`, and `DISK_SIZE_GB`—to match your workload and budget constraints. Once executed, the VM will come online ready to accept SSH connections and have the necessary CUDA toolkit preinstalled.
